followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the reported 15–16 July 2020 customs-service admission interruption and the observed reopening day. The phase concerns approaching/new cargo requiring South African customs facilities. Already admitted trucks continued processing with Mozambican help. Broad journalistic closure wording cannot erase that explicit exception or prove all passengers were stopped. The closure day 15 July and reported restoration day 16 July support a one-calendar-day difference and the existing day-precise complete/exact flags. The 13:00 SMS is announced timing; the 15:59 update is a status-post timestamp, not a first restored vehicle clock or exact elapsed-hour duration. Human disease control is supported by the SARS spokesman’s disinfection explanation after a positive staff test. The report’s varying staff labels do not alter the qualified generic official description. The decisive 16 July reopening update was freshly read. The initial report, reproduced SARS advisory and indexed UNECE entry were reused with original access limits. Reproduced notices and embedded social posts are not automatically independent observations. Original R06 authorship is disclosed. The accepted B02 row exactly matches the frozen guard and PIDA S10, -25.44311 / 31.98674. It locates the named crossing area while preserving approaching-cargo scope and unspecified direction, with a scoped interval. It is not the yard entrance or disinfection-room position.
